# Adjie Brotosukmono

> Adjie Brotosukmono is an Indonesian energy economics consultant and power system engineer at Mott MacDonald in Perth, Western Australia. Adjie holds a Bachelor's and a Master's degree in Electrical Power Engineering from Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), and has also worked in online education and in banking.

Canonical site: https://www.adjiebrotots.com/
Full story: https://www.adjiebrotots.com/about/
Also known as: Harso Adjie Brotosukmono (full name), Adjie Brotot (nickname), adjiebrotot (handle)
Based in: Perth, Western Australia, Australia. From Indonesia.
Languages: English, Bahasa Indonesia
Contact: adjiebrotots@gmail.com, https://www.linkedin.com/in/adjiebrotot/

## Who Adjie is, in short

- Current role: Energy Economics Consultant at Mott MacDonald in Perth. The work sits where power engineering meets economics: electricity market modelling, and testing whether wind, solar, battery and network projects stack up.
- Also: a power system engineer and a project manager by experience.
- Education: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), Indonesia. Bachelor's and Master's in Electrical Power Engineering, both on full scholarships.

## Career, in order (no dates on purpose)

1. University at ITB, Bandung. Joined the Scholarion Exchange (Japan), the ASEAN Young Leaders Program (Singapore, and later Cambodia), the Young ASEAN Leaders Policy Initiative (Thailand, twice) and the 30th International Youth Forum (Seoul, South Korea). Interned at E-Life Solutions Sdn. Bhd. in Johor, Malaysia, developing ERMA, software for managing electromagnetic risk.
2. Online teaching at Quipper and Pahamify, two Indonesian edtech companies, before graduating. Taught physics and became an Academic Lead (a project management role) before leaving.
3. Bank Central Asia (BCA), Jakarta: a blend of IT, finance and project management.
4. Merz Consulting, a Perth energy consultancy: Power System Engineer. First exposure to the Australian grid and its mine sites.
5. Mott MacDonald acquired Merz Consulting. Adjie relocated to Perth as an Energy Economics Consultant. The job was advertised locally first, as Australian law requires, and asked for a power system engineer with banking and finance experience.
